title: Balance Point Index
statement:
You get an array of integers nums. An index i is a balance point when the sum of everything strictly to its left equals the sum of everything strictly to its right. The element at i itself belongs to neither side. An empty side sums to 0.

Return the leftmost balance point, or -1 if there is none.

examples.why: Left of index 2: 3 + 1 = 4. Right of it: 2 + 2 = 4.
At the last index the right side is empty (0), and the left side is 1 + (−1) = 0. Negative numbers make this possible.
Every index balances; return the leftmost one.

hints: Recomputing both side sums for every index costs O(n) each. What do you already know when you move from index i to i + 1?
The right sum is the total minus the left sum minus the current element.
Compute the total once. Walk left to right with a running left sum; index i balances when left === total − left − nums[i]. Add nums[i] to left after the check.

explain.intuition:
For each index you need two sums: what is to its left and what is to its right. Recomputing them every time is O(n²). But the three parts, left, the element itself and right, always add up to the same total. So once you know the total and keep a running left sum, the right sum is simply total − left − nums[i].

This is the prefix-sum idea in its smallest form: one pass to learn the total, one pass with a running sum. Scanning from the left and returning at the first hit gives the leftmost answer for free.
steps: Compute total, the sum of all elements.
For each index i: if left === total − left − nums[i], return i.
pitfalls: Adding nums[i] to left before the check. Then the element is counted on the left side.
Assuming the answer cannot be the first or last index. An empty side sums to 0, as in [1, -1, 4].
Using two pointers that move towards each other. With negative numbers, the sums do not grow in one direction, so that greedy idea breaks.

solutions.title: Sum both sides for every index
solutions.idea: For each index, add up everything on the left and everything on the right, and compare.

solutions.title: Total plus running left sum
solutions.idea: The right side is total − left − nums[i], so one running sum is enough.

followups: Return every balance point instead of the leftmost.
